findings.text: follow-on: the retarget rewrites target_id and evidence but not target_units (or cocos_label), which were taken from the model entry for the original structure path. For a value binding the two paths share a unit, so this is latent; for a source_property=time binding the retargeted .../current/time carries units s while a model-supplied target_units of A for .../current is now checked against it by validate_mapping (validation.py:143-155), which can raise a spurious "Units incompatible" or "Identity transform but units differ" escalation against a binding the retarget just corrected. The tests leave target_units None, so the interaction is not covered.

follow-on: the _DD fixture declares pf_active/circuit/current as a STRUCTURE with neither data nor time child, but the live DD gives that path a data child (verified via a bounded graph query), so the no-data-child branch is exercised only against a fabricated graph and no real path backs it; the fixture's comment at line 59 asserts a DD shape that is false, which could mislead a future reader.

follow-on: _STRUCTURE_DATA_TYPES re-defines the structure-type set already canonical at imas_codex/core/node_classifier.py:44 (STRUCTURE_TYPES), adding a third copy beside the IN ['STRUCTURE','STRUCT_ARRAY'] literals in build_dd.py and tools/graph_search.py; reusing the existing constant would keep one definition of "a structure".

justifications.durability: The declared negative control removes the retarget and reproduces 3 failures at exit 1, so the rewrite behaviour is guarded. Three gaps remain. (1) _retarget_structure_bindings rewrites only target_id and evidence (mapping.py:1707-1711); it does not refresh target_units or cocos_label, which were taken from the model entry for the original structure path (mapping.py:1778). For the value case the units coincide (both A on .../current and .../current/data), but for a time binding the retargeted .../current/time carries units s while the model's target_units for .../current was A, so validate_mapping's unit check (validation.py:143-155) can raise a spurious "Units incompatible"/"Identity transform but units differ" escalation against a binding the retarget just corrected. (2) STRUCT_ARRAY is accepted as a structure type (mapping.py:1655) but the retarget forms the literal p + '/data' child, and no test exercises an array target, so whether an array's value container is named data is unverified. (3) The no-data-child branch is not exercised against any real DD path (see the test-fixture finding).
justifications.evidence: I ran both arms and the negative control myself in this session. Base arm at 0ea3c2c5c from a scratch extraction with PYTHONPATH shadowing the editable install: 576 passed, 5 skipped, 7 deselected, EXIT=0 (base-tests-ids.log, module.__file__ under /tmp/base-review.UpmpRU). Head arm at c792d5d1a (the reviewed change merged) with PYTHONPATH=$PWD: 580 passed, 5 skipped, 7 deselected, EXIT=0 (head-tests-ids.log). The delta is exactly the 4 new tests in test_binding_data_target.py and no failure appears in either arm. The negative control reproduces independently: removing the _retarget_structure_bindings call reddens test_value_binding_on_a_structure_retargets_to_its_data_child, test_time_binding_on_a_structure_retargets_to_its_time_child and test_structure_without_a_data_child_is_refused, 3 failed 1 passed, EXIT=1 (review-negative-control.log), matching the reviewed run's own negative_control.log. The reviewed manifest declares no baseline_suite, so I derived the base arm rather than trusting the run's single after_suite-equivalent line. I also verified the retarget Cypher against the live graph (bounded, three named paths), since the unit test mocks gc and cannot exercise it: the query returned pf_active/coil/current data_type STRUCTURE with data+time children, legitimately reaching the retarget.
justifications.fit: The change reuses the existing escalation machinery (EscalationFlag / EscalationSeverity.ERROR) rather than inventing a second refusal channel, and it sits inside validate_mappings beside the existing section guard, before validation, so no new pipeline stage is added. The helpers are named for what they do (_structure_children, _retarget_structure_bindings) and the test module is named for the behaviour (test_binding_data_target). No plan, sprint or ticket identifier appears in any symbol, comment, docstring or the test module name.
justifications.goal_fidelity: §24's three behaviours are all present. _retarget_structure_bindings (mapping.py:1680-1726) rewrites a binding whose target data_type is STRUCTURE/STRUCT_ARRAY to the structure's data child (mapping.py:1707), or to its time child when source_property == 'time', and records the rewrite in binding.evidence (mapping.py:1708-1711); a structure lacking the required child is refused as an EscalationSeverity.ERROR (mapping.py:1713-1724); a binding already naming a leaf is returned unchanged (mapping.py:1700-1702). It is wired before the section guard and validation (mapping.py:1790), so the guard and validate_mapping run against the final path. All four named tests pass. The one goal-side gap is target_units/cocos_label, which the retarget leaves as the model supplied for the structure path (see durability).
justifications.reuse: The retarget runs one batched Cypher over the distinct targets (mapping.py:1658-1678) rather than a query per binding, which is the right shape. Two reuse gaps: _STRUCTURE_DATA_TYPES (mapping.py:1655) re-defines a set already canonical at imas_codex/core/node_classifier.py:44 as STRUCTURE_TYPES, adding a third copy beside the IN ['STRUCTURE','STRUCT_ARRAY'] literals in build_dd.py and tools/graph_search.py:2344; and _structure_children queries data_type plus child existence, overlapping check_dd_paths (tools.py:212-236), which is called moments later by validate_mapping — the two could share one path lookup.
justifications.scope_discipline: The commit's three changed paths (imas_codex/ids/mapping.py, tests/ids/test_binding_data_target.py, docs/evidence/fragments/jt60sa-mapping-study-expansion/binding-targets-data-field.html) are exactly the run's three declared write paths, and git show --stat lists no fourth path.
